info.description: The Saleson API allows you to perform all the operations that you do with our web client. SalesOn API is built using REST principles which ensures predictable URLs that makes writing applications easy. # Overview The SalesOn API likely refers to APIs used to integrate the [SalesOn field sales management software](https://www.google.com/search?q=SalesOn+field+sales+management+software&oq=SAleson+APi&gs_lcrp=EgZjaHJvbWUqBggAEEUYOzIGCAAQRRg7MgkIARAAGA0YgAQyCAgCEAAYDRgeMggIAxAAGA0YHjIGCAQQRRg8MgYIBRBFGEEyBggGEEUYPDIGCAcQRRhB0gEIMzQ5M2owajeoAgiwAgHxBdWE3frLkcco&sourceid=chrome&ie=UTF-8&mstk=AUtExfCM8NqYqx6g1scI_atK52kcjqJ2GXdcqUf_yc3u82jl1SMhM7pst0aVMiFGvr3vFiWq9w67wCw6zZo18Vms6EsmwhHw9zxWv1WMyyPZVRb0zk3v9kieUy3MlfU46bkhTeOknHLg1laEN1Iwh8FtxMDm4FfrEgJIuZiOQzW1mdHuZws&csui=3&ved=2ahUKEwi16tju3NKPAxUDzzgGHXfpIEgQgK4QegQIARAC) with other systems, such as [ERP software](https://www.google.com/search?q=ERP+software&oq=SAleson+APi&gs_lcrp=EgZjaHJvbWUqBggAEEUYOzIGCAAQRRg7MgkIARAAGA0YgAQyCAgCEAAYDRgeMggIAxAAGA0YHjIGCAQQRRg8MgYIBRBFGEEyBggGEEUYPDIGCAcQRRhB0gEIMzQ5M2owajeoAgiwAgHxBdWE3frLkcco&sourceid=chrome&ie=UTF-8&mstk=AUtExfCM8NqYqx6g1scI_atK52kcjqJ2GXdcqUf_yc3u82jl1SMhM7pst0aVMiFGvr3vFiWq9w67wCw6zZo18Vms6EsmwhHw9zxWv1WMyyPZVRb0zk3v9kieUy3MlfU46bkhTeOknHLg1laEN1Iwh8FtxMDm4FfrEgJIuZiOQzW1mdHuZws&csui=3&ved=2ahUKEwi16tju3NKPAxUDzzgGHXfpIEgQgK4QegQIARAD), for purposes like managing sales orders, tracking salesman location, and handling invoicing. The SalesOn platform itself uses APIs for its mobile app and to connect to other business tools. # Company Id In SalesOn, your business is termed as an company. If you have multiple businesses, you simply set each of those up as an individual company. Each company is an independent SalesOn company with it’s own company ID, base currency, time zone, language, contacts, reports, etc. The parameter company_id along with the company_id should be sent in with every API request to identify the company. The company_id can be obtained from the GET /company API’s JSON response. # **API Call Limit** API calls are limited to provide better quality of service and availability to all the users. You can make 100 requests per minute per organisation. The limits on total requests per day are listed below for each plan: - Free Plan - 1000 API requests/day - Standard Plan- 2000 requests/day - Professional Plan- 5000 requests/day - Premium Plan- 10000 requests/day - Elite Plan- 10000 requests/day - Ultimate Plan- 10000 requests/day

request.description:
### **Overview**

This HTTP PATCH request is used to update the details of a company. The request should include a JSON payload with the following fields:

### **Arguments**

**name** (string)

The name of the company.

**mobile** (string)

The contact number of the company.

**email** (string)

The email address of the company.

**type** (string)

The type of the company, e.g., MANUFACTURER.

**gstin** (string):

The Goods and Services Tax Identification Number of the company.

**address** (string):

The address of the company.

**supply_place** (string)

The supply place of the company.

**office_timing** (object)

The office timing of the company, with start and end time.

**working_day** (object)

The working days of the company, with boolean values for each day.

**bank_details** (array of objects)

The bank details of the company, including account number, account holder name, bank name, branch name, and IFSC code.

**holidays** (array of objects)

The holidays of the company, including the name and date of each holiday.

item.description:
### Overview A price list is a document that lists the prices of goods or services offered for sale. It can be a physical document or a digital list, and it may include additional information like descriptions, images,Custom prices and contact details . - **Purpose:**Price lists are used to communicate pricing to customers, allowing them to easily compare prices and make informed decisions. - **Content:**They typically include the name of the item, a description, the MRP, the custom price and sometimes additional details like type, measurements, or relevant terms. - **Usage:**Businesses use price lists to manage pricing, track profitability, and offer discounts or special rates to different customer segments or sales orders. - **Benefits:**Price lists can simplify the buying process for customers, help businesses streamline pricing management, and facilitate communication between buyers and sellers. ### Arguments **name**(string) The name of the pricelist **description**(string) A detailed information of pricelist **type**(string) The type of pricelist eg. fixed, markup and markdown **status**(boolean) The status of the pricelist whether it is active or deactive **products**(string) The item for which pricelist to be created **product id**(number) Products unique number **rate**(number) The custom price of the product to be filled in price list | **End points** | | --- | | PATCH /products/price-list/price-list_id
POST /products/price-list/price-list_id
GET /products/price-list
GET /products/price-list/price-list_id
DELETE /products/price-list/price-list_id |

This endpoint retrieves the Latest Physical Stock of Party

#### Request

- Method: GET
    
- URL :

#### Response

The response of this request is a list of all Latest Physical Stock of Party containing all details like id,company_id,name,description,type,status,updated_by,erp_id,created_at and updated_at

item.description:
Physical stock refers to the actual inventory items physically present and available in a business's warehouse or store. It's the actual quantity of goods on hand, as opposed to theoretical or accounting stock levels. This is often verified through a physical inventory count, where items are manually counted and recorded. **Key aspects of physical stock:** - **Actual inventory:**It represents the real quantity of goods physically in the warehouse, not just what's recorded in the books. - **Physical verification:**It's often determined by a physical inventory count, where items are manually counted and recorded. - **Inventory management:**Understanding physical stock is crucial for managing inventory levels, ensuring accuracy, and optimizing warehouse operations. I**n contrast to accounting stock:** - **Accounting stock:**Represents the stock levels as reflected in accounting records, based on transactions like purchases and sales. - **Difference:**There can be discrepancies between accounting stock and physical stock due to errors, damage, theft, or other factors, highlighting the importance of regular physical counts. **Examples of physical stock scenarios:** - **Retail store:**The actual number of shirts on the shelves or in the backroom represents physical stock. - **Warehouse:**The number of pallets of raw materials or finished goods stored in the warehouse constitutes physical stock. **Importance of physical stock:** - **Accurate inventory records:**Ensures that inventory records accurately reflect the actual stock levels. - **Avoid stockouts:**Helps to prevent stockouts by identifying potential shortages before they occur. - **Reduce losses:**Identifies discrepancies and losses due to damage, theft, or other issues, allowing for corrective actions. - **Improve operations:**Enables more efficient warehouse operations and better inventory management practices. | **End points** | | --- | | POST /products/physical-stock
PUT /products/physical-stock/physical-stock-id
GET /products/physical-stock/latest |

### Overview Its is an inventory that to be sold. A product is **an object or a system that is made available for consumer use through the process of marketing**. Product widely means literally anything that can be offered in a market keeping its demand in close connection. **something that is made to be sold**, esp. something produced by an industrial process or something that is grown or raised through farming. For Example Amul milk, Aashirwad atta and Almond etc #### Attributes **group_name**(string): The group name of product. **brand_name**(string): The brand name of product. **images**: The image to be upliaded of product. **bulk_prices**(number): The bulk price of product. **sp_with_gst**(number): Selling price with Gst of product **pp_with_gst**(number): Purchase price with gst of product **id**(number): The unique id of the Product **company_id**(number): The unique company id. **name**(string): The name of product. **description**(string): The Description of product. **product_code**(number): The code of product. **sub_category_id**(number): The sub category of product **hsn**(number): HSN code is a 8-digit uniform code classifying over 5000+ products **gst**(number): The GST to be applied on product. **unit**(number): The unit in which the product to be measured. **stock**(number): The total number of product available . **low_stock**(number): The quantity of product is less **purchase_price**(number): The purchase price of product to purchase that product **mrp**(number): The mrp of product **sell_price**(number): The selling price of product request.description:
### Create Transaction

This endpoint allows to create the transactions

### Attributes

- **type**():The type of transaction to be created eg. sales invoice ,sales order etc.
    
- **party**(object) **:**
    
    - **party_id**(integer) The id of party
        
    - **name**(string):The mobile number of an party holder
        
    - **mobile**(integer):The multiplier of the pri unit
        
    - **address**(string):The address of party located
        
- **products**(object):
    
    - **free_qty**()**:** The quantity of product which given free to party in sales
        
    - **gst**(): The gst tax applied on product
        
    - **hsn**() : The hsn number of product
        
    - **name**(): The name of product
        
    - **product_id**():The product id is a unique identifier to identify the product
        
    - **quantity**(): The qunatty is the number of product added in sales
        
    - **sell_price**(): The selling price is a price to sale the product
        
    - **unit**():The Unit of product in which it is measured
        

### Request

- Method :POST
    
- URL:{{host}}transactions/sales-invoice
    
- { "party" : { "party_id": 11558, "address": "Nehru Road", "mobile": "9876543210", "name" : "Sample Trader" },  
    "products": \[ { "free_qty": 0, "gst": 5, "hsn": "9603", "name": "Aashirwad atta1", "product_id": 19683, "quantity": "1", "sell_price": 50, "unit": "Gms" } \], "type": "Sales Invoice"}
    

### **Response**

The response of this request is a JSON schema containing the information of created transaction

### Update Transaction

This endpoint allows to update the transactions

### Attributes

- **type**():The type of transaction to be created eg. sales invoice ,sales order etc.
    
- **party**(object) **:**
    
    - **party_id**(integer) The id of party
        
    - **name**(string):The mobile number of an party holder
        
    - **mobile**(integer):The multiplier of the pri unit
        
    - **address**(string):The address of party located
        
- **products**(object):
    
    - **free_qty**()**:** The quantity of product which given free to party in sales
        
    - **gst**(): The gst tax applied on product
        
    - **hsn**() : The hsn number of product
        
    - **name**(): The name of product
        
    - **product_id**():The product id is a unique identifier to identify the product
        
    - **quantity**(): The qunatty is the number of product added in sales
        
    - **sell_price**(): The selling price is a price to sale the product
        
    - **unit**():The Unit of product in which it is measured
        

### Request

- Method :POST
    
- URL:{{host}}transactions/sales-invoice
    
- { "party" : { "party_id": 11558, "address": "Nehru Road", "mobile": "9876543210", "name" : "Sample Trader" },  
    "products": \[ { "free_qty": 0, "gst": 5, "hsn": "9603", "name": "Aashirwad atta1", "product_id": 19683, "quantity": "1", "sell_price": 50, "unit": "Gms" } \], "type": "Sales Invoice"}
    

### **Response**

The response of this request is a JSON schema containing the information of updated transaction

item.description:
### Overview a warehouse refers to a place or space where goods are stored before they are sold or distributed. It's a crucial component of the supply chain, linking production with the end consumer or retailer. Warehousing ensures that products are available when needed, minimizing delays and optimizing inventory management. **Function of a Warehouse in Sales:** - **Storage:**Warehouses store raw materials, components, or finished products, waiting for them to be needed for sale or use. - **Inventory Management:**Warehouses track and manage inventory levels, ensuring products are readily available to meet demand. - **Order Processing:**Warehouses facilitate order fulfillment, picking, packing, and shipping products to customers or retailers. - **Distribution Hub:**Warehouses serve as distribution centers, where products can be redistributed to retailers, wholesalers, or directly to consumers. - **Efficiency and Cost Reduction:**Efficient warehousing operations can reduce costs by optimizing inventory, minimizing storage space requirements, and streamlining shipping processes. **Importance of Warehouses in Sales:** - **Ensuring Availability:**Warehouses are essential for ensuring that products are readily available to meet customer demand, preventing stockouts and improving customer satisfaction. - **Optimizing Supply Chains:**Warehouses play a vital role in optimizing supply chain operations, ensuring the efficient movement of goods from production to consumption. - **Supporting Online Sales:**In the age of e-commerce, warehouses are critical for managing online orders, picking, packing, and shipping products directly to customers. In essence, a warehouse is a vital link in the sales process, ensuring that products are available when needed, optimizing inventory, and streamlining the distribution of goods to customers or retailers. ### Attributes **warehouse_id**() The unique Identifier for warehouse given by server **product_id**() The products id **stock**() The product quantity to be added **rate**() The price of the product **name**(string): The name of warehouse **email**(string): The email address of warehouse to which any one contact **mobile**(integer): The mobile number of warehouse **address**(string): The address of warehouse **gstin**(string): 15 digit GST identification number of the customer **place_of_supply**(string): Place where the goods/services are supplied to. **status**(booliean): The status of the warehouse whether it is active or inactive **is_primary**(string): The warehouse is primary or not will be checked by this field **is_billing_address**(string): The address where goods are supplied **party_id**(): The unique identifier for party provided by server **page_size** ()**:** The page size for store list of warehouses | **End point** | | --- | | POST /warehouses

item.description:
### Overview A typical expense is incurred when money goes out of your pocket. Whether its a product you buy from your vendor to run your business, or food that you eat while on business trips, it’s important to track the money you spend. In simple terms, expenses are costs that are paid out, typically for goods or services. They represent the money spent by an individual or business to operate, acquire something, or meet obligations. Here's a more detailed explanation: - **Cost:** Expenses are essentially costs associated with something. - **Outflow of Money:** They represent money leaving a person's or business's possession. - **For Goods or Services:** Expenses are incurred when acquiring something of value, like a product or a service. - **Examples:** Common expenses include Bank Fee and Charges ,RAW materials, Repair & Maintenance, Telephone & Internet Expense, Transportation & Travel Expense, rent, utilities, salaries, and the cost of goods sold. - **Business vs. Personal:** Businesses track expenses for accounting and tax purposes, while individuals may track expenses for budgeting. ### Attributes **category_id**(integer): The category of expense **user_id**(integer): The user id of expense **payment_mode**(string): The payment mode of expense **payment_date**(integer): The payment date of expense - **products**(object):Individual payment details - **name**(integer)**:** name of the expense. Search expense by expense name - **tax**(integer): The tax amount of expense - **quantity**(integer): The quantity of item - **price**(integer):The price of item - **attachment**(): The image to be uploaded to attach the expense | **End points** | | --- | | POST /expenses

item.description:
### Overview This report features that allow users to view and analyze sales data. These reports can be customized and filtered to provide insights into various aspects of sales performance, such as daily sales, monthly sales by product, and overall sales trends. **Customization and Filtering:** - **Data Selection:** It will allow you to select specific data points to include in your reports, such as specific products, transaction, party , payments, purchase.users ,production and sales. - **Reporting Time Periods:**You can usually generate reports for specific time frames, like daily, weekly, monthly, or quarterly. - **Filtering:**You can often filter reports based on various criteria, such as invoice type, order status, route, user, party ,warehouse or product categories,product brans and many more. **Types of Reports:** - **All Transaction Reports:**These reports provide a overview of all transaction including details like the number of transactions, total revenue, and top-selling products. - **Sales Reports:**These reports offer a more comprehensive view of sales performance over a longer period, allowing for trend analysis. it includes [Sales By Party](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/sales-by-party), [Item Sales By User](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/item-sales-by-user), [Sales By User](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/sales-by-user), [Sales By Item](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/sales-by-item), [Sales By Category](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/sales-by-category), [Sales By Brand](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/sales-by-brand), [Van Sales By Item, ](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/van-sales-by-item) [Van Sales Reconciliation By Item etc](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/van-sales-reconcilation-by-item) EndFragment - **Product-Specific Reports:**These reports focus on the sales performance of individual products, providing insights into their profitability and popularity.it will also include [Stock Summary, ](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/stock-summary) [Item details, ](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/product-details) [Rate List](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/rate-list), [Stock Adjustment](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/stock-adjustment), [Low Stock Summary, ](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/low-stock-summary) [Stock Summary By Brand](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/stock-summary-by-brand), [Stock Summary By Category ](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/stock-summary-by-group) etc - **Users Reports:**These reports track the performance of individual SAles representative. This also includes [User Summary](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/user-summary), [Attendance](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/user-attendance) and [Activity Log](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/user-activity) allowing you to see their Name, Check In, Check Out, Total Visit,| Visit Out of Range, Distance (km), Working Hr etc - **Purchase Reports:**These reports offer a purchase data, allowing you to identify name of purchased product and [Purchase By Party](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/purchase-by-party), [Purchase By Item, ](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/purchase-by-item) [Purchase By Brand details](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/purchase-by-brand) - **Payment Reports:** These reports shows the details information of payments recieved , [Payment Detail, ](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/payment-detail) [Payment Received By User, ](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/payment-received-by-user) [Payment Received By Party, ](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/payment-received-by-party) [Payment Mode](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/payment-made) - **Production Reports:**These reports shows the imformation of [Production Detail By Item](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/production-detail-by-item)[Production Raw Materials](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/production-raw-material) - **Party Reports:**These Reports focus on the party performance of indivisual party providing details of [Party Wise Outstanding](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/party-outstanding), [Party Statement](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/party-statement), [Distributor Statement, ](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/distributor-statement) [Supplier Statement, ](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/supplier-statement) [Party Last Visited](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/party-last-visited), [Party Visited](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/party-visited), [Party Not Visited](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/party-not-visited), [Party Added By User and ](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/party-added-by-user) [Party Transaction by Item.](https://staging.saleson.co.in/report/party-transaction-by-product) | **End points** | | --- | | GET /reports/stock-summary

item.description:
### Overview A target refers to a predefined goal or objective, typically expressed as a specific amount of revenue or units to be sold within a given timeframe. It serves as a benchmark for measuring performance and motivating sales teams to achieve business objectives. **Here's a more detailed explanation:** - **Sales Target as a Goal:**A sales target is a concrete, measurable objective that a sales team or individual aims to achieve within a specific period, such as a day, month, quarter, or year. - **Purpose:**Setting sales targets helps in several ways: - **Performance Measurement:** It provides a clear standard against which to evaluate the effectiveness of sales efforts. - **Team Motivation:** Targets can act as motivators, encouraging salespeople to push for higher sales figures. - **Strategic Alignment:** Targets can be aligned with broader business goals, ensuring that the sales team is working towards the overall strategic vision. - **Setting Targets:**Targets can be set based on various factors, including: - **Historical Sales Data:** Analyzing past performance to project future sales. - **Market Conditions:** Considering market trends, competition, and potential opportunities. - **Company Objectives:** Aligning targets with the overall revenue and growth goals. - **Examples:** - A company might set a target to generate $100,000 in revenue from new sales in the next quarter. - A sales team might be given a target to close 20 new deals by the end of the month. - **Types of Targets:**Sales targets can be expressed in different ways, such as: - **Revenue Target:** Focusing on the total monetary value of sales. - **Unit Target:** Focusing on the number of products or services sold. - **Customer Acquisition Target:** Focusing on the number of new customers gained. - **Importance:**Sales targets are crucial for driving sales performance, guiding marketing efforts, and ultimately contributing to the overall success of a business. | **End points** | | --- | | POST /targets
